6. a) Kurt A. Frank 
c) State Senator 7th Senatorial District
d) 25
e) Stated he is concerned with noise pollution and the orderly displacement of people who live in the path of the proposed freeway corridor.
f) Indicated that the existing freeway g) noise is at a constant high level and will greatly be increased by adding the Airport Spur and aircraft as the Airport Spur and aircraft at the airport expands. Since the amount of noise will be greater it will be hard to instruct students in Hamlin-Garland School.
The relocation law should be administered to prevent a hardship for those in the path of the freeway.
As shown on the graph on page 122, the range of noise levels varies considerably throughout the day. See page 150 for proposed highway noise abatement.

Senator Frank has also commented by letter on the Draft EIS. His letter and responses are found on pages 206 thru 210.
See pages 143 and 144 for a response.
7. a) John Plewa 
c) State Representative 20th Assembly District
d) 29
e) Stated that the 1972 EIS is no longer valid because of the increase in noise levels from traffic and the opening of the East-West Runway at Mitchell Field.
f) the 1972 Draft EIS is no longer valid since the noise levels are higher with increased highway traffic and the opening of Runway 7R-25L.
g) The writing of any environmental impact statement of this magnitude requires approximately one year to write and another two months for printing, shipping, and federal and state agency review before an environmental impact hearing can be held. At this point in time, therefor, the measured data necessary to start writing the statement would be a minimum of fourteen months old.
